extDescription.message: Keep your proxy on and let the current website connect directly with one click.

statusSavedOff.message: Saved, but Saved sites is off

rememberNeedsOn.message: Turn on Saved sites (top right) first

errInvalidDomain.message: Enter a valid domain or URL (no wildcards).

errProxyScheme.message: The protocol must be HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5.

errProxyHost.message: Enter only a host name or IP, without protocol or port.

errProxyPort.message: The port must be a whole number from 1 to 65535.

errOtherExtension.message: Another extension (e.g. ZeroOmega) controls the proxy. Disable it first.

errPolicy.message: The proxy is locked by an organization policy.

errNotApplied.message: Direct rules are not applied yet. Reopen this window.

errTab.message: The current tab could not be found.

errTooMany.message: You can save up to 500 sites.

errNoResponse.message: The extension did not respond. Reload it on the extensions page.

secProxyDesc.message: The local address of your proxy app (Clash, v2rayN …). Sites that are not direct use it.

optFallback.message: Go direct if the proxy is unreachable

optFallbackDesc.message: Keeps the browser usable when your proxy app is not running.

optPrivateDesc.message: localhost, private IPs and single-label host names.

optReloadDesc.message: Turn off if you switch while filling in forms.

secSavedDesc.message: While on, these sites always connect directly. While off, the list is kept but ignored and only “this time” switching works.

emptySaved.message: No saved sites yet. On a website, open the popup and turn on “Always connect directly”.

secTempsDesc.message: Each ends when the tab that started it closes, or when the browser restarts.

how1.message: The extension gives the browser a small local PAC script: listed sites go DIRECT, everything else goes to the proxy above. Only this browser profile is affected — Windows proxy settings and other apps are not touched.

how2.message: With no direct rules active, the extension hands proxy control back and the browser follows the system proxy as usual. The background worker sleeps when idle; nothing stays resident.

how3.message: Rules work per domain, so other tabs of the same site connect directly too. If your proxy app runs in TUN / virtual adapter mode, browser DIRECT cannot bypass it — add a DIRECT rule in the proxy app instead.

how4.message: Logins and videos are sometimes served from other domains. If only part of a page fails, include the whole site or add those domains here.

portWarn.message: Must match your proxy app’s port! If it is wrong, other sites cannot reach the proxy while a site is set to direct.

portHelpTitle.message: Why is a proxy port needed?

portHelp1.message: An extension cannot change one site and leave the rest as they were — it can only replace the browser’s proxy configuration as a whole. Once in control, it must decide the route for every site. It also cannot read the Windows system proxy, so you tell it your proxy app’s port and every other site keeps using the proxy.

portHelp2.message: The extension only takes control, and uses this port, while a site is set to direct. Otherwise the browser follows the system proxy as usual.
